A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCT research. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison after matching renamed and relocated sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original Type I/II error simulations, causal-discovery experiments, robustness studies, and a Big Five Personality data analysis in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix E, including the simulation results and real-data graph comparison.

M1.justification: The binarization, bridge-equation covariance estimation, nodewise regression, and asymptotic testing pipeline remain the same. The added pseudocode documents that pipeline; the exposition and local formula corrections do not establish a substantive redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian simulations, non-Gaussian and nonlinear settings, graph-density variations, and Big Five Personality variables. The additional experiments move from Appendix C to Appendix E without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Fisher-Z and chi-square retain their respective roles in the reported comparisons. Fisherz_nodis remains the continuous-data reference in the main causal-discovery experiments. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, conditioning-set sizes, discretization levels, graph-generation settings, calibration, PC-to-DAG conversion, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Removing the duplicate data-generation paragraph from v3 Appendix B does not remove the settings retained in Section 4.2.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the sample-size and conditioning-set sensitivity studies, non-Gaussian/nonlinear robustness experiments, denser-graph analysis, nonzero-mean/non-unit-variance experiment, and real-data case study. Their questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,500 repetitions for the error-rate experiments and 10 graph instances with different seeds for the stated causal-discovery settings. Mean/standard-deviation reporting and plotted uncertainty remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–9 retain the same result panels, plotted values, error bars, and discovered graphs. The accompanying numerical and qualitative findings are also unchanged; relocated appendix figures do not constitute new results.

T1.justification: v4 corrects the cutoff indexing in Equation 1, the mixed-pair estimating-equation index, and the CI variance-expression summation bound from n to p−1. Appendix B.1 expands the conditional-variance proof step. Lemma 3.7 restates nodewise-regression relationships already present in v3 rather than adding a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: testing latent-variable CI despite discretization, handling discrete/mixed/continuous pairs, deriving asymptotic distributions, and demonstrating effectiveness empirically. The added implementation link is an access disclosure.

C2.justification: The Gaussian-assumption discussion, nonlinear failure example, and robustness interpretation move from v3 Section 3.4 to v4 Appendix B.9.2. Binarization-related information loss, limited small-sample power, and interpretations of the graph and real-data results remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds an implementation URL in the abstract and Algorithm 1 in Appendix D, documenting data selection, covariance assembly, and testing steps. It removes v3's attribution of the implementation to Zheng et al. (2023). Hardware, runtime, and experimental settings remain documented as before.

R1.justification: The Zheng et al. (2023) Causal-learn citation and bibliography entry are removed with the implementation-attribution paragraph. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to Fan et al. (2017) and other CI methods are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: The central method exposition is substantially reworked: Section 3 introduces notation, Section 3.1 separates boundary estimation and covariance recovery with expanded explanations, and nodewise-regression properties receive a lemma presentation. Notation is standardized, the assumption discussion moves into the proofs appendix, and new notation and pseudocode appendices reorganize the documentation.

P2.justification: v4 adds a notation table spanning Appendix A and a formatted Algorithm 1. Figure 4 is repositioned after removal of the duplicate data-generation paragraph, and surrounding material reflows. The existing figures retain their graphical content, axes, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the existing method easier to follow through clearer covariance-estimation explanations, consolidated notation, computational steps, and implementation access information, while correcting several mathematical indices. These are modest usability gains. The new pseudocode leaves the scaling between its raw coefficient and Theorem 3.8's sqrt(n)-scaled distribution unclear, and removal of the Causal-learn attribution weakens provenance; these shortcomings limit the improvement.
